note: Inclusive/exclusive comparisons in src/engine that no test holds.
A boundary is 'held' when flipping <= to < (or >= to >) makes a test fail. On
2026-08-30 forty-seven of sixty-eight were not held, which is what this file
records. Only a NEW entry fails the check -- the backlog is a backlog, not a
monthly alarm, and an alarm that always fires is not an alarm.
This list should SHRINK. Several of these are statutory thresholds where 'at or
below' is the rule and the difference is a real answer to a real person:
benefits.ts        the ACA 400% FPL cliff, and the 100% FPL floor below which
no premium tax credit is allowed
iraDeduction       the phase-out endpoints, where landing on the low end means
a full deduction and the high end means none
educationCredits   the same shape for the AOTC and Lifetime Learning ranges
garnishment.ts     which of the two federal limits binds, on a tier-3 screener
Others are defensive guards (`if (amount <= 0) return 0`) where the boundary is
not a decision anybody experiences. Both kinds are listed, because deciding
which is which is a reading, and a list that pre-filtered by someone's reading
would hide the one they got wrong.
